title: Completed-coefficient direct image preserves derived completeness
statement: Fix distinct primes p,l and a finite extension E/Q_l. Let f:X to Y be any scheme morphism and let c:R_Y to f_*R_X satisfy c followed by f_*pi_X,n = pi_Y,n followed by the canonical finite constant-section map, for every positive quotient [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For any RightImage F of the actual module pushforward along c [def-pur-completed-pushforward-models], if K in D(R_X) is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], then F(K) in D(R_Y) is derived complete. All scheme, hom and coefficient universes remain independent.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (1),(4), with normalized strict-tower comparison

proof.text: Identify quotient-tower derived completeness with the local principal-uniformizer criterion. The forward implication uses the strict Roos triangle and quotient completion. For the reverse implication choose a termwise-flat K-flat representative, use the principal-cone/quotient comparison, and transport the strict Roos triangle with its augmentation. This extracts the datum-independent part of the existing Roos/intrinsic argument; no new coefficient datum is chosen.

source.place: Tags 0A0E and 099B, principal Koszul completion; proetale.tex Tag 099N (1),(3)

proof.text: Choose a K-injective complex J representing K. Its scalar endomorphism mu is multiplication by the actual uniformizer section. The principal completion unit of J is a quasi-isomorphism. Principal cone levels, their countable product, and its shifted cone are K-injective, so this quasi-isomorphism is a homotopy equivalence. Any additive functor therefore sends it to a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0A0E and 099B, principal Koszul completion; proetale.tex Tag 099N (1),(3)

proof.text: Module pushforward preserves countable products: after the fully faithful module-sheaf forgetful functor, evaluate on each site object, where it is source evaluation followed by scalar restriction and both preserve products. Its termwise additive functor commutes with mapping cones and shifts. The cone comparisons are natural for the (mu,1) transition squares, and the product comparison conjugates one-minus-shift. Hence direct image of the principal completion is isomorphic, as a complex, to the principal completion of the image scalar.

proof.text: The finite projection equations imply compatibility of c with the constant-to-completion map. Evaluate the constant sheafification unit equation on the uniformizer to identify the transported scalar with the actual target scalar. The local principal criterion makes its principal completion complete. Transport through the preceding isomorphism, the image of the source unit, and the K-injective computation isomorphism supplied by RightImage F.

lean.statement:
theorem directImage_preservesComplete (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hlp : l ≠ p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (c : R l E Y ⟶ (ringPush.{t, u} f).obj (R l E X))
    (hc : ∀ n, c ≫ (ringPush.{t, u} f).map (projection l E X n) =
      projection l E Y n ≫ finiteStructure l E f n)
    [hpush : (push f c).Additive] (F : RightImage (push f c))
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod X (R l E X)))
    (hK : IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E X K) :
    IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E Y (F.functor.obj K)
